name: SMS-AI
title: A Vue front end for AI teaching templates with streamed answers and a chatbot
role: Frontend developer (Vue 3), plus prompt engineering and model training for domain-specific workflows
summary: The Vue 3 front end of an AI assistant inside a student management system: teachers fill in templates such as lesson plans or worksheets and the answer streams in live, with a real-time chatbot and a history of results. I also built the admin UI for configuring chatbots.

metrics.label: signed-in screens: templates, runner, chatbot, history
LLM providers to choose from (GPT-4, Gemini)

problem: Teachers needed classroom material from structured prompts without writing prompts themselves. Every template has its own fields, so forms couldn't be hard-coded, and LLM answers take long enough that waiting for the full response feels broken.

constraints.label: Schema-driven forms
constraints.text: The backend sends each template's fields, response type, response count and whether the model can be chosen, and the form renders from that.

constraints.label: Streaming output
constraints.text: Answers arrive over a WebSocket in chunks and have to appear as they come in.

architecture.caption: The template's fields render from its schema, the request goes out over a WebSocket, and the answer streams into Vuex and renders as Markdown.

sections.heading: Templates, chatbot and history
paras: Each template page builds its inputs (dropdown, textarea or text), an optional choice between OpenAI and Gemini and a counter for up to 3 results. The chatbot uses its own socket channel, and history views list past runs and chats as Markdown.
For the chatbot admin I built bot creation (name, language, prompt, logo, response length), knowledge-file upload from disk or a link, grid and list file views, preview and editing in TinyMCE.

challenges.title: Building streamed answers in the store
challenges.text: Each incoming frame goes to Vuex and is appended to the current message; the message counter only moves on when the backend signals the stream is complete, so partial chunks never become separate messages.

outcome: Teachers sign in, pick a template, choose the model, watch answers stream in and review earlier results, all on one Vue 3 + Vuex + Tailwind codebase talking to the AI backend over REST and WebSockets.
